title: Deployed Contract Ingestion - verified-only (V2.6.1)
description: Reference shape for scripts/ingest_onchain.py's output record (docs/decisiones.md D-055). This script NEVER makes a network call - it only normalizes an ALREADY-FETCHED JSON blob (see #/definitions/rawInput) describing one (address, network) pair, obtained by some tool OUTSIDE this Skill. Like report-schema.json, this document is the authoritative human/AI-facing reference; it is not executed by a JSON Schema library at runtime (scripts/ingest_onchain.py is a hand-written, standard-library-only script).

address.description: Lowercase-normalized only. EIP-55 mixed-case checksum verification is deliberately NOT performed (rule R-I4) - null when the input address was not well-formed (see completeness.reasons, code INVALID_ADDRESS).

name.description: Null for an unrecognized-but-still-numeric chainId (never blocks ingestion - rule R-I3), or when chainId itself is null.

verified.description: As reported by whatever explorer/tool produced the raw input. False is a transparency fact, never itself a vulnerability finding (rule R-I1).

hasCode.description: Null when the raw input did not report it. False means the queried address has no deployed bytecode at all (EMPTY_BYTECODE) and takes precedence over any verified/sourceFiles claim.

virtualPathPrefix.description: "onchain://<chainId>/<address>/", used to build each recovered source file's path in `bundle`. Null when address or network could not be resolved (IDENTITY_INCOMPLETE). CAVEAT (rule R-I5): preprocess.py's own, unmodified normalize_path() collapses the doubled "//" down to a single "/" once this bundle is actually parsed - the REALIZED systemGraph/contract key ends up "onchain:/<chainId>/<address>/...", not byte-identical to this prefix.

bundle.description: A multi-file bundle in preprocess.py's own, unmodified "=== FILE: ... ===" / "=== END FILE ===" format, ready to pipe into preprocess.py's stdin unchanged - only when verified=true, hasCode is not false, and at least one source file survived safety checks. Null otherwise.

sourceFileCount.description: Number of source files actually included in `bundle`.

skippedSourceFiles.description: Every rejected source file, with why - never a silent drop (rule R-I6).

completeness.description: Same {status, reasons[{code, detail}]} shape preprocess.py's own `completeness` and report-schema.json's `scope` already use (rule R-I7) - not a new, parallel vocabulary.

provenance.description: Per-field origin tag: "on-chain" (a direct, already-performed RPC read - e.g. hasCode), "explorer" (third-party-reported - e.g. verified, sourceFiles, contractName, compilerVersion), or "analyzer-inferred" (computed by this script - e.g. virtualPathPrefix). Never a blanket single tag for the whole record (rule R-I2) - different facts genuinely have different origins within one ingestion.

note.description: Fixed English sentence restating the hard rule: verified=false (or any completeness limitation) is never a vulnerability by itself (rule R-I1).

runtimeStateNote.description: Fixed English sentence: this record never carries live storage/balances/tx history - deployed runtime state stays out of scope (see docs/legal-risk-register.md RISK-014, as clarified by D-055).

rawInput.description: The ALREADY-FETCHED JSON this script consumes - never produced by this Skill itself. address and network are required; everything else is optional and missing fields simply narrow what can be ingested (never an error).

network.description: A chain id (number or numeric string), a recognized network name (e.g. "ethereum", "polygon"), or {"chainId": N}.

businessRules: R-I1: `verified: false` (or any other completeness limitation this script records) is a transparency fact about what could be recovered, never a vulnerability finding or signal on its own - this script has no code path capable of emitting a finding/signal at all.
R-I2: provenance is tagged per field (on-chain / explorer / analyzer-inferred), never as one blanket tag for the whole record.

R-I3: an unrecognized-but-numeric chainId is always accepted (name stays null) - only a genuinely unparseable `network` value fails ingestion; this script never blocks on an incomplete chain registry.

R-I4: address normalization is lowercase-canonicalization and basic well-formedness only. EIP-55 checksum verification is not performed - it requires Keccak-256, unavailable in Python's stdlib (hashlib.sha3_256 is the different, NIST-finalized SHA3-256 and would silently produce a wrong checksum).

R-I5: contract identity for recovered source is the virtual path "onchain://<chainId>/<address>/<file>", fed to preprocess.py as a bundle (never as a real file on disk, never via any preprocess.py code change). preprocess.py's own unmodified normalize_path collapses the doubled slash to a single one - the realized key is "onchain:/<chainId>/<address>/<file>#Contract", not byte-identical to the constructed prefix.

R-I6: a source file is rejected (path traversal, absolute path, control characters, duplicate-after-normalization, or content shaped like a bundle boundary marker) only ever WITH a recorded reason in skippedSourceFiles - never a silent drop.

R-I7: completeness reuses preprocess.py's/report-schema.json's own {status: complete|partial|failed, reasons: [{code, detail}]} shape verbatim, so it can be propagated (e.g. into an eventual report's scope/categoryCoverage NOT_ASSESSED reasoning) without translation.
R-I8: this script never modifies preprocess.py, score.py, validate_report.py, the detectors registry, or config/modes.json, and never makes an HTTP/RPC call itself.
